title: A regression's time limit starts when it has the machine (GitHub issue #8)
objective: A regression that waited for a machine slot or for the whole machine still gets the full devloop.regression_timeout_seconds for its run, counted from the moment the slot or the machine is taken.
outline: devloop/regression.py verify(): keep `slot = take(cfg, began + cfg.regression_timeout_seconds)` for the wait; after a slot came, compute `deadline = time.time() + cfg.regression_timeout_seconds` and pass it to _verify; in _verify, preflight gets `timeout=max(1, min(600, deadline - time.time()))` instead of the fixed 600. Docstring lines 10-12. README '## Machine slots' (the two sentences named in the acceptance, about lines 185 and 199). tests_devloop/test_machine.py: the two README asserts. core/slots.py does not change.

notes: Group new-g1: the operations fixes (#8, #10, #11), none of which touches the DAG; #11's ticket also edits regression.py and depends on this one. Decision (opener): the wait reuses regression_timeout_seconds rather than a new devloop.regression_wait_seconds, as the request allows when a setting fits: another group's regression runs at most that long once it has the machine, and VISION asks for no new setting without removing one. acceptance: devloop/regression.py verify(): the wait for the slot (slots.take) or for the whole machine (slots.take_machine) stays limited by devloop.regression_timeout_seconds counted from the start of the wait (as today); once the slot or machine is taken, a new deadline = that moment + regression_timeout_seconds is the only limit of the run: preflight (at most 600 s and never more than the time left), quick, full and the flaky rerun (second_look) all share it. No new setting is added (the wait reuses regression_timeout_seconds, see notes).

Slot case: board/config.json devloop machine_slots 1, regression_timeout_seconds 10, tests.full = 'sleep 4; <fake_tests.py> full'; the test holds slot-0 (core.slots.take) and releases it after 7 s; `python3 devloop/regression.py --branch main --out F` exits 0 and F has status 'green'. Whole-machine case: the same with machine_slots 2 and regression_exclusive true, the test holding slot-0 for 7 s: exit 0, status 'green'. (Today, measured: exit 2, unmeasured, the same summary.)

Preflight shares the run's limit: tests.preflight = 'sleep 6; <fake_tests.py> preflight', regression_timeout_seconds 3, no machine_slots: exit 2, F status 'unmeasured', F summary contains 'tests.preflight' and 'timeout'. A wait that runs out is unchanged: with the only slot (or a slot, in exclusive mode) held for the whole run and regression_timeout_seconds 2, the regression exits 2 after at least 2 s with status 'unmeasured' and a summary saying it never got the slot or the machine, as today; the existing cases T3Acceptance.test_a_regression_without_a_slot_in_its_time_is_unmeasured and ExclusiveRegression.test_a_regression_without_the_whole_machine_is_unmeasured_and_releases (tests_devloop/test_machine.py) pass unchanged.

The regression.py module docstring says the wait is limited by regression_timeout_seconds and the run gets its own regression_timeout_seconds from when the slot (or the machine) is taken; it no longer says the wait, quick and full all count against regression_timeout_seconds.

devloop/README.md '## Machine slots': the sentence starting "A regression's wait still counts against `regression_timeout_seconds`" and the sentence starting "The whole wait counts against `regression_timeout_seconds`" are replaced. ## Issue #8: a regression's deadline starts when it has the machine
Observed in T (2026-11-23): g57's full regression waited for the machine behind g56, then had about 10 minutes left; the unit layers ran 554 s, test_browsers was stopped at the deadline after 40 s and the run was `unmeasured`.
Today devloop/regression.py `verify()` passes `began + regression_timeout_seconds` to `take`/`take_machine` and gives `_verify` the time left, so the wait is charged to the run (the module docstring says so).
Wanted: `regression_timeout_seconds` limits the run from the moment the slot or the whole machine is taken (preflight, quick, full and the flaky rerun share it). The wait for the machine gets its own limit: reuse an existing setting if one fits, otherwise add `devloop.regression_wait_seconds` with a default long enough for a full regression of another group to finish (say so in devloop/README.md); a wait that runs out is `unmeasured` with a summary saying it never got the machine, as today. Update the docstring.

## Issue #10: pages close when their subject is handled from any path
Observed in T (2026-11-23): the board showed 35 open pages, every one already answered or superseded: a group's "unmeasured" page after `actl tickets rerun gN`, tickets' "stuck" pages after `actl tickets ready N`, a fixer question after the group was readied, every `created` page.
Wanted:
- An action on a subject (a ticket or a group), through any path (CLI, board, `actl new --revise ... --decision`, `tickets ready`, `tickets rerun`, `tickets release`, `cancel`), acks every open decision/env page of that subject that the action answers, recording `acked_by` as the path (e.g. "tickets ready").
- When a subject moves on by itself (a stuck ticket is running again, an unmeasured group runs a regression again, a group or ticket lands or is cancelled), its older decision/env pages are acked with `acked_by: "superseded"`.
- `created` pages are information: the board's 要你判 tab and the waiting count do not count them (they stay listed in `tickets inbox`).
- Opener: grep every place that writes or reads `acked`, and every test that asserts pages stay open; list the tests that change.

## Issue #11: a controller restart does not kill in-flight regressions
Observed in T (2026-11-23 13:52Z): stopping `actl run --forever` and starting it again left g58 and g59 with "regression unmeasured - None" pages and no regression.py running; the g57 auto_fixer survived and was adopted. Jobs are started by osx.spawn with start_new_session=True, so the cause is not known.
Wanted: first reproduce it with the loop harness (start a controller, let it start a regression with a slow fake `full`, stop the controller with SIGTERM and with SIGINT, start a new one) and find the cause; write it in the ticket. Then fix it so a running regression survives the restart and is adopted like an auto_fixer: the new controller waits for it and reads its result. If the cause turns out to be outside A (for example how the user stopped the process on macOS), say so and make the controller report it instead of writing "unmeasured - None" (the page names what happened to the job).
